rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: a piece that defends another has a job. A forcing move, such as a check or a capture, can pull it away from its post. This blow is called a deflection.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.e2: This position comes from a game played on Lichess, and Black is to move. The knight on f2 attacks your bishop on g4, and only the king on e3 defends the knight.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.p: Find the forcing move that pulls the white king away from defending the knight.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.certo: The bishop gives check on c5. The king must leave e3, and from no free square does it keep defending the knight on f2.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the bishop check on c5: the king must leave e3, and from no free square does it keep defending the knight on f2.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.err.g4d7.1: The bishop steps out of the attack, but the king still defends the knight on f2, and Black wins nothing.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.err.g4d7.2: With this move, White has a resource: the knight goes to d3, next to the king, and now watches c5.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.err.g4d7.3: Back to the position: look for the check that forces the king to leave e3.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.err.g4f5.1: The bishop steps out of the attack to f5, but the king still defends the knight on f2, and Black wins nothing.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.err.g4f5.2: With this move, White has a resource: the pawn goes to g4, defended by the knight, and attacks your bishop again.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.err.g4f5.3: Back to the position: look for the check that forces the king to leave e3.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not pull the king away from the knight. Look for a check.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the forcing move against the king on e3.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.l1: White must answer the check. No white piece can block it, and the king has to move.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.l2: On d2 the king no longer reaches f2, and the knight is left without a defender.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.l3: The bishop captures the loose knight. The check deflected the king, and the knight it guarded fell.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex1.l4: In positions like this, look at each defender and ask: if it leaves its post, what is left loose? A forcing move can make it leave.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: now with White, and the deflection comes through a capture. Your queen attacks the rook on d5, and only the black queen on d8 defends it.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.p: Find the capture that pulls the black queen away from defending the rook.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.certo: The bishop captures the pawn on e7 and attacks the queen and the rook on f8. If the queen captures the bishop, it leaves d5.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.revela: The capture is the bishop on e7: it attacks the queen and the rook on f8, and Black cannot save both.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.err.b3d5.1: The queen captures the rook on d5, but the black queen defends it from d8.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.err.b3d5.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen on d8 recaptures on d5, and White gives the queen for a rook.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.err.b3d5.3: Back to the position: look for the capture that attacks the queen on d8.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.err.f1d1.1: The rook goes to the d-file, but the queen on d8 still defends the rook on d5, and Black gains time.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.err.f1d1.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen goes to d7, still defends the rook on d5 and now defends the pawn on e7.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.err.f1d1.3: Back to the position: look for the capture that attacks the queen on d8.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not pull the queen on d8 away from the rook. Look for a capture that attacks the queen.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the capture that attacks the black queen.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.l1: The black queen is attacked and must decide. If it keeps defending d5, the rook on f8 falls.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.l2: The queen captures the bishop on e7 and leaves the d-file: the rook on d5 is left without a defender.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.l3: The queen captures the loose rook. White gave a bishop and won a rook and a pawn.
rot.deflection.ideia.ex2.l4: In positions like this, the deflection does not need a check: a capture that attacks the defender also forces it to choose.
rot.deflection.demos.partida.1: Attack: White again. The queens attack each other, and trading them wins nothing. But only the king on c8 defends the black queen on d7.
rot.deflection.demos.partida.2: The bishop captures the pawn on b7 with check. It is a forcing move: the king must respond.
rot.deflection.demos.partida.3: The king captures the bishop and leaves c8. On b8 it would be the same: the queen on d7 would also be left without a defender.
rot.deflection.demos.partida.4: The queen captures the loose queen. White gave a bishop and won the queen.
rot.deflection.demos.garfo.1: Attack: now with Black. The white bishop on d5 has only one defender, the king on c4.
rot.deflection.demos.garfo.2: The knight gives check on e3 and attacks the bishop: it is a fork. The king must leave c4.
rot.deflection.demos.garfo.3: The king steps out of check and attacks the knight. To keep defending the bishop it would need d4, but the pawn on c5 watches that square.
rot.deflection.demos.garfo.4: The knight captures the loose bishop and escapes the king. The forking check deflected the only defender.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.1: Attack: with White. The queens attack each other, and trading them wins nothing. A check can deflect a defender, but which piece defends the black queen?
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.p: Find the check that pulls the defender of the queen on c5 away from its post.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.certo: The rook gives check on d8. The rook on c8, which defends the queen, is the piece that can capture it.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.revela: The right check is the rook on d8: the piece that can capture it is the rook on c8, the same one that defends the queen.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.err.e5h8.1: The queen gives check on h8, but the king it pulls from g8 was not defending the queen on c5.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.err.e5h8.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the king captures the queen, and the rook on c8 keeps defending the queen on c5.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.err.e5h8.3: Back to the position: look for the check that forces the rook on c8 off the c-file.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.err.e5c5.1: The queen captures the queen on c5, but the rook on c8 defends it.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.err.e5c5.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the rook recaptures on c5, and the queens leave the board with no material won.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.err.e5c5.3: Back to the position: look for the check that forces the rook on c8 off the c-file.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.2: The king has no free square, and Black must capture the rook or block the check.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.3: The rook on c8 captures the rook and leaves the c-file. Putting the queen on f8 would also lose material: the rook would capture it with check.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.4: The queen captures the loose queen. White gave a rook and won the queen.
rot.deflection.demos.excecao.5: In positions like this, find the defender before the deflection. Pulling the wrong piece away, like the king to h8, only gives away material.
rot.deflection.pratica.valeAqui.enunciad: Now with Black. Your queen attacks the rook on e2 and the pawn on g2. Before you move, find who defends them. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.deflection.pratica.valeAqui.fim: Your bishop captured on g2 and attacked the bishop on f1. When it recaptured, it left the rook on e2 without a defender, and the queen captured it.
rot.deflection.pratica.valeAqui.err.g4g2: The queen captures on g2 with check, but the bishop on f1 recaptures, and you give the queen for a pawn. The bishop on f1 defends the rook and g2: pull it away with another piece.
rot.deflection.pratica.valeAqui.err.h5h4: That move does not use the bishop on f1, which defends the rook on e2 and the pawn on g2 at once. Look for the move that forces it to choose.
rot.deflection.pratica.valeAqui.err.e8a8: The rook moves, but the bishop on f1 still defends the rook on e2 and the pawn on g2. Look for the move that forces it to choose.
rot.deflection.pratica.valeAqui.err.g8h7: That move does not use the bishop on f1, which defends the rook on e2 and the pawn on g2 at once. Look for the move that forces it to choose.
rot.deflection.pratica.valeAqui.err.g4e2: The queen captures the rook on e2, but the bishop on f1 recaptures. First pull the bishop away from defending the rook.
rot.deflection.pratica.torre.enunciado: Black again. The queens attack each other. Before you move, find the defender of the white queen. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.deflection.pratica.torre.fim: The rook gave check on e1, and the rook on d1 captured it. Without its defender, the queen on d3 was loose, and your queen captured it.
rot.deflection.pratica.torre.err.f3d3: The queens are traded, and the rook on d1 recaptures: you win no material. Look for a check that pulls the rook on d1 away from its post.
rot.deflection.pratica.torre.err.f3g4: The queen avoids the trade, but the rook on d1 still defends the queen on d3. Look for a check that pulls it away from its post.
rot.deflection.pratica.torre.err.f3f2: The queen captures the pawn on f2 with check, but the king recaptures.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.enunciado: Now with White. Before you move, find the piece that defends the black queen. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.fim: The bishop gave check on e5, and the bishop on b2 captured it. The black queen was left without a defender, and your queen captured it.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.err.c4c1: The queens are traded, and the bishop on b2 recaptures: you stay a rook down. Look for a check that pulls the bishop on b2 away from its post.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.err.c4d5: The queen stops attacking the queen on c1, and the deflection loses its target. Look for a check that pulls the bishop on b2 away from its post.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.err.c4f7: The queen stops attacking the queen on c1, and the deflection loses its target. Look for a check that pulls the bishop on b2 away from its post.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.err.c4e4: The queen stops attacking the queen on c1, and the deflection loses its target. Look for a check that pulls the bishop on b2 away from its post.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.err.c4e6: The queen stops attacking the queen on c1, and the deflection loses its target. Look for a check that pulls the bishop on b2 away from its post.
rot.deflection.pratica.bispo.err.c6c7: The pawn advances, but the black queen captures your queen on c4.
